title: Argumentation for Common Ground: Finding Zones of Possible Agreement between Individuals in Conflict
abstract: arXiv:2608.15634v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How can common ground between societies in conflict be identified when citizens' acceptability of peace agreements is shaped by contested narratives? Such acceptability is mediated not only by the clauses that agreements include or exclude, but crucially by citizens' subjective reasoning concerning agreements' clauses. In this paper, we leverage computational argumentation to introduce a novel approach to identifying mutually acceptable agreements among individuals in conflict, i.e. a Zone of Possible Agreement (ZOPA). First, we introduce a quantitative bipolar argumentation framework tailored to represent each side's reasoning about peace agreements. We then show how merging these frameworks can enable negotiators to identify peace agreements that are mutually acceptable. translated_title: 寻求共识的论证：在冲突个体之间找到可能的协议区间
translated_abstract: 摘要：当公民对和平协议的接受度受到争议性叙事的影响时，如何识别冲突社会之间的共同点？这种接受度不仅受协议包含或排除的条款所调节，更重要的是受公民对协议条款的主观推理所影响。在本文中，我们利用计算论证引入了一种新方法，用于识别冲突中个体之间相互可接受的协议，即可能的协议区间（ZOPA）。首先，我们引入了一个定量的双极论证框架，专门用于表示每一方对和平协议的推理。然后，我们展示了如何合并这些框架，使谈判者能够识别双方都能接受的和平协议。为了在现实相关条件下评估我们的方法，我们聚焦于巴以冲突，其中长期存在的政策、实践者和公众……
tldr: 本文通过定量双极论证框架，提出了一种识别冲突个体间相互可接受协议（ZOPA）的新方法，并以巴以冲突为例进行验证。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a novel approach using quantitative bipolar argumentation frameworks to identify mutually acceptable agreements (ZOPA) between individuals in conflict, demonstrated on the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
